title: Tennis Match Ends at 3:34 AM! Shelton Beats Alcaraz in a Five-Set Thriller
summary: Imagine staying up until 3:34 in the morning to watch a tennis match. That's what happened at the US Open in New York! Ben Shelton, from the USA, played Carlos Alcaraz from Spain in a quarter-final match that started at about 11 PM. It was so exciting that nobody wanted to leave. The match lasted four hours and 28 minutes! That's longer than two big movies back-to-back. In the end, Shelton won in five sets: 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6. The last set was a super close tie-break, where you have to win 10 points. Shelton said it was "the most enjoyable match that I've had in my career." He had never beaten Alcaraz before—in fact, he had lost to him three times. And he had never beaten a top-three player in 17 tries. But this time, he did it! The crowd gave him a standing ovation. This win means Shelton will play Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals. That's a big deal because it guarantees an American man will be in the final for the first time in 23 years. The last American man to win the US Open was Andy Roddick in 2003, when Shelton was less than a year old! Alcaraz was sad but proud of how he fought. He said, "I leave the court with a smile, healthy." What a match!
why_it_matters: The match is a reminder that you can keep trying even after losing to the same person again and again — one night can change everything.
